item.title: Google unveils TurboQuant, a lossless AI memory compression algorithm — and yes, the internet is calling it ‘Pied Piper’
item.description: Google’s TurboQuant has the internet joking about Pied Piper from HBO's "Silicon Valley." The compression algorithm promises to shrink AI’s “working memory” by up to 6x, but it’s still just a lab experiment for now.

item.title: Melania Trump wants a robot to homeschool your child
item.description: The first lady sees AI and robotics playing a prominent role in the future of American education.

item.title: Bernie Sanders and AOC propose a ban on data center construction
item.description: Senator Bernie Sanders and Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez introduced companion legislation to halt construction on new data centers until Congress passes comprehensive AI regulation.

item.title: Google launches Lyria 3 Pro music generation model
item.description: Google is launching Lyria 3 Pro, an upgraded music model that generates longer, more customizable tracks, as it expands AI music tools across Gemini, enterprise products, and other services.

item.title: Reddit takes on the bots with new ‘human verification’ requirements for fishy behavior
item.description: Reddit will require suspected automated accounts to verify they’re human, as it ramps up efforts to curb bot-driven spam and manipulation.

item.title: Harvey confirms $11B valuation: Sequoia triples down
item.description: Investors like Sequoia, Andreessen Horowitz, Kleiner Perkins, and Elad Gil can't get enough of AI legal tech startup Harvey.

item.title: Granola raises $125M, hits $1.5B valuation as it expands from meeting notetaker to enterprise AI app
item.description: Granola's valuation jumped from $250 million to $1.5 billion with this round, and it has added more support for AI agents after users previously complained.

item.title: Meta launches new initiative to support entrepreneurship, drive AI adoption
item.description: Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg said in a memo to staff that small businesses have always been a big part of the company's business model, and that while tens of millions of entrepreneurs already use its platforms to grow and connect with customers, the company wants to do more in the space.

item.title: Meta turns to AI to make shopping easier on Instagram and Facebook
item.description: Meta is using generative AI to provide more product and brand information to consumers when they're shopping in its apps.

item.title: With Sift, two ex-SpaceX engineers are bringing the software that helped launch rockets to the factory floor
item.description: Sift is building the data infrastructure for advanced manufacturing.

item.title: Lucid Bots raises $20M to keep up with demand for its window-washing drones
item.description: Lucid Bots has seen demand accelerate over the last year for its window-cleaning drones and power-washing robots.

item.title: With $3.5B in fresh capital, Kleiner Perkins is going all in on AI
item.description: The fundraise includes $1 billion for investing in early-stage startups and $2.5 billion for late-stage growth businesses.

item.title: OpenAI’s Sora was the creepiest app on your phone — now it’s shutting down
item.description: Though the underlying Sora 2 video- and audio-generation model is scarily impressive, there was not sustained interest in an AI-only social feed.

item.title: Kentucky woman rejects $26M offer to turn her farm into a data center
item.description: A "major artificial intelligence company" reportedly offered a Kentucky family $26 million to build a data center on their farm.

item.title: Anthropic hands Claude Code more control, but keeps it on a leash
item.description: Anthropic’s new auto mode for Claude Code lets AI execute tasks with fewer approvals, reflecting a broader shift toward more autonomous tools that balance speed with safety through built-in safeguards.

item.title: Spotify tests new tool to stop AI slop from being attributed to real artists
item.description: The idea behind the new tool is to give artists more control over which tracks are associated with their name on Spotify.

item.title: Databricks bought two startups to underpin its new AI security product
item.description: With an overflowing war chest from its recent $5 billion raise, Databricks is buying startups and looking for more. It acquired Antimatter and SiftD.ai.

item.title: Arm is releasing the first in-house chip in its 35-year history
item.description: Arm is producing its own CPU for the first time. It developed the CPU with Meta, which is also the chip's first customer.

item.title: OpenAI’s plans to make ChatGPT more like Amazon aren’t going so well
item.description: OpenAI says it's moving away from Instant Checkout, which allowed users to buy items directly through the ChatGPT interface.

item.title: Google TV’s new Gemini features keep fans updated on sports teams and more
item.description: Three Gemini-powered features are coming to your Google TV. This includes visual responses, deep dives, and sports briefs.
